newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Stolid Sing dlr brushes off polls.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Stolid Sing dlr brushes off polls.

text.p: * Singapore dollar remains on even keel after ruling People's Action Party wins all but two seats in parliament.
* Malaysian ringgit makes slight gains on unwinding of long dollar positions and ringgit/Sing cross play but volume thin.
* Indonesian rupiah holds steady amid ample liquidity and uncertainty about the central bank's fixing policy and a possible band widening.
* Thai baht firms in line with weaker dollar. Interbank rate slips as money flows back into market after holidays.
The Singapore dollar remained typically stolid as players returned after a two-day break for New Year's Day and general elections on Thursday.
The ruling People's Action Party (PAP) was guaranteed a majority in parliament well before any votes were cast as opposition parties contested only 36 of the 83 seats.
But forex dealers said the market showed little reaction to what turned out to be the PAP's best general election result in 16 years, as the opposition lost two of its four seats.
"It's been very quiet. But the consensus is that the market is looking for a stronger U.S. dollar against the Sing dollar after the election," said a U.S. bank dealer.
He said the U.S. dollar appeared to have formed a good base around S$1.3985/90 and looked set to head back above S$1.4000.
Renewed interest in the ringgit/Sing cross would also keep the Sing dollar under pressure, he said. "People are going back into the ringgit/Sing cross for the yield carry."

Across the border, the Malaysian ringgit gained slightly from some unwinding of long dollar positions by Malaysian banks but dealers said volumes remained low and ranges thin in the absence of Tokyo players and lacklustre interest from other centres.
They said the announcement of a 1.5 billion ringgit issue of Bank Negara bills next week was providing some support.
"The issues mean interest rates will remain around the present levels or go higher," said a dealer, adding that this would attract funds seeking higher yields.
The Indonesian rupiah remained stable amid ample liquidity and uncertainty over the central bank's fixing policy and the possibility of a band widening in the new year.
A local bank dealer in Jakarta said there was some dollar buying from Singapore operators up to a high of 2,362.5 at the opening, but this was later countered by local selling.
Spot rupiah was quoted at around 2,361.50/62.50 at 0430 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,361.80/62.30.

"They want to see whether the central bank will proceed with the three- to four-point depreciation it has pursued in the past two to three months," the dealer said, noting that it depreciated the rupiah by only two points last week..
He said speculation on a band-widening was another factor preventing operators from buying dollars aggressively despite sustained ample rupiah liquidity.
"People are a bit nervous they'll widen the band in the first quarter. Some positions are already being built into that," said the Singapore dealer.
In Thailand, the baht gained from the dollar's weakened tone against the majors although overall activity remained slow.
The overnight interbank rate came off to 12.00 percent in early trade as money withdrawn before the New Year holiday returned to the market, dealers said.
"Money withdrawn ahead of the holiday is returning. Some banks are heard quoting about 11 percent," a dealer at Thai Danu Bank said.
He said upward pressure on interbank rates had also eased due to a slowdown in dollar buying after the U.S. unit slipped against other major currencies.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Boonrith Ratanavaraporn in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
